---
title: Cursor Origin
description: Use pull requests on Cursor Origin, including stacked pull requests, reviews and check runs.
icon: i-simple-icons-cursor
---

The Cursor Origin provider covers pull requests on Origin, including stacked pull requests, with their comments, reviews and check runs. It also covers repository contents and Origin App installations. Origin has no issues, discussions, releases or notifications.

::note
The Cursor Origin provider is experimental. It uses the alpha Origin API `v1alpha1` (`ORIGIN_API_VERSION`), which can change. See [Capabilities](/concepts/capabilities).
::

## Authentication

The provider accepts a user access token or Origin App credentials:

```ts
import { cursorOrigin } from 'forges/cursor-origin'

const forge = cursorOrigin({
  auth: { type: 'token', token: process.env.CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN! },
}).create()

const app = cursorOrigin({
  auth: {
    type: 'app',
    appId: 'app_01...',
    privateKey: process.env.ORIGIN_APP_PRIVATE_KEY!,
    installationId: 'i_01...',
  },
}).create()
```

A user access token is the value that the Origin CLI reads from `CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN`. Personal Cursor API keys aren't Origin bearer tokens, and the provider doesn't accept them.

For app auth, `privateKey` is the app's Ed25519 private key in PKCS#8 PEM format. The provider signs an app JWT with it. With `installationId`, the provider mints installation tokens as it needs them. Without `installationId`, the provider authenticates as the app itself. In that case, `installations.list()` lists the app's installations, and `installations.provider(installation)` returns a provider for one installation.

Origin has no anonymous access, so `auth` is required.

## Instance

The instance is `origin.cursor.com`, which is the host in clone URLs. `baseUrl` defaults to `https://api.cursor.com`, and the provider appends `/v1/origin`.

## Stacked pull requests

For a pull request in a stack, `thread.stack` contains the stack ID and the parent pull request.

## Merging

Origin supports the `merge` and `squash` methods only. If you don't pass `method`, `merge()` reads the repository settings. When exactly one method is allowed, it uses that method. When both are allowed, it throws `MergeMethodRequiredError`. `whenChecksPass` and `message` are unavailable.

## Review comments

A comment anchored to a line in the diff is a review comment. Review comments appear in `threads.events()` as `review_comment` events, and `threads.comments()` doesn't return them. Origin doesn't link inline comments to the review that submitted them, so each review has `comments: false`.

## Webhooks

Origin sends webhooks in the Standard Webhooks format, with these headers:

| Header | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `webhook-id` | The delivery ID |
| `webhook-timestamp` | The time of the delivery, in seconds |
| `webhook-signature` | An Ed25519 signature over the hex SHA-256 of `<webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<body>` |

The provider verifies the signature against the public keys from the `/keys` endpoint, which it caches for ten minutes. It doesn't use `webhookSecret`. It rejects deliveries with a timestamp more than five minutes from the current time.

```ts
const forge = cursorOrigin({ auth }).create()

const events = await forge.webhooks.ingest({
  headers: request.headers,
  body: await request.text(),
})
```

`installation.*` deliveries become `installation` events. You register hooks in the app definition, so the `webhooks` management methods are unavailable.

::contributing{title="Record Cursor Origin fixtures" to="/contributing/record-fixtures"}
```sh
CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN=... FIXTURE_CURSOR_ORIGIN_REPO=owner/repo \
FIXTURE_CURSOR_ORIGIN_PULL=1 pnpm record-fixtures cursor-origin
```
::
